label: History
value: Anne Shirley was born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia.
unit: Anne Shirley was born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia, to schoolteacher parents who both died of fever shortly after her birth. Raised in hardship by various foster families and an orphan asylum, she was mistakenly brought to Green Gables in Avonlea, Prince Edward Island, by Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert, who had wanted a boy. Despite the mistake, they decided to keep her. Anne quickly formed a passionate, lifelong friendship with her neighbor Diana Barry. She attended Avonlea school, where an academic rivalry with Gilbert Blythe began after he called her 'Carrots' and she smashed her slate over his head. Anne excelled in her studies, eventually tying with Gilbert for first place on the Island-wide entrance exams for Queen's Academy. After a year at Queen's, she won the Avery Scholarship, but gave up going to college to stay at Green Gables and teach at Avonlea when Matthew died and Marilla's eyesight threatened to fail. During her two years as a beloved Avonlea schoolma'am, Anne organized the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, helped raise the orphaned Keith twins at Green Gables, and formed a deep friendship with the romantic Miss Lavendar Lewis. When Marilla's friend Mrs. Rachel Lynde came to live at Green Gables, Anne was able to resume her studies and attended Redmond College in Kingsport alongside Gilbert, Priscilla Grant, and new friend Philippa Gordon. At Redmond, Anne was courted by the wealthy, handsome Roy Gardner, but eventually realized he was not her true ideal and rejected his proposal. Returning home after graduating with High Honors in English, Anne suffered through a night of anguish when Gilbert fell dangerously ill with typhoid fever, realizing then that she loved him.

label: History
value: Aunt Jamesina agreed to move to Kingsport
unit: Aunt Jamesina agreed to move to Kingsport to keep house for her niece, Stella Maynard, and her college friends Anne Shirley, Priscilla Grant, and Philippa Gordon at Patty's Place. She brought along her two cats, Joseph and the Sarah-cat, and eventually adopted Rusty as well. She presided over the household with humor and indulgence, refusing to strictly discipline the girls and instead letting them manage themselves. After the girls graduated, she decided to stay at Patty's Place with her cats instead of traveling or visiting relatives, remaining there to keep the house warm until they returned or moved on.

label: History
value: Billy Andrews grew up in Avonlea.
unit: Billy Andrews grew up in Avonlea as a member of the Andrews family. He attended local school gatherings and concerts, often admiring Anne Shirley from afar with silent devotion. Due to his extreme shyness, he enlisted his sister Jane to propose marriage to Anne on his behalf after his father granted him the upper farm in his own name. Following Anne's prompt rejection of the proposal, Billy suffered no lasting heartbreak and instead married Nettie Blewett, with whom he 'appeared out' at the Avonlea church shortly thereafter.

label: History
value: Leonora Bowman entered the service of Miss Lavendar Lewis at Echo Lodge when she was thirteen years old.
unit: Leonora Bowman entered the service of Miss Lavendar Lewis at Echo Lodge when she was thirteen years old, following her three older sisters who had previously served in the same role. Because her predecessors had all been called Charlotta by Miss Lavendar, she was dubbed 'Charlotta the Fourth.' When Anne Shirley and Diana Barry accidentally stumbled upon Echo Lodge, Charlotta welcomed them and assisted Miss Lavendar in entertaining them. She formed a deep admiration for Anne, attempting to mimic her graceful mannerisms. When Stephen Irving returned to courtship with Miss Lavendar, Charlotta eagerly supported the romance and helped prepare for the wedding. Following the marriage of Stephen and Miss Lavendar, Charlotta relocated to Boston with them to continue her service.

label: History
value: Davy Keith and Dora are twins.
unit: Davy Keith and his twin sister Dora were orphaned when their mother, Mary Keith, died of consumption. Their distant relative Marilla Cuthbert took them into Green Gables for the winter at Anne's urging. Davy quickly established a reputation for chaotic mischief, dropping a caterpillar down a girl's neck at church, locking his sister in a toolhouse, and dropping a toad into Marilla's bed. Despite his wild pranks, Anne's loving approach and patience helped him learn right from wrong, particularly when he confessed to telling falsehoods and promised never to do so again. Upon the death of his uncle, Richard Keith, a trust fund was established for Davy and Dora, allowing them to remain permanently at Green Gables. Davy enrolled at Avonlea School, where he formed a friendship with Milty Boulter and gradually reformed his mischievous behavior, growing deeply attached to Anne and Marilla.

Despite his wild pranks, Anne's loving approach and patience helped him learn right from wrong, particularly when he confessed to telling falsehoods and promised never to do so again. Upon the death of his uncle, Richard Keith, a trust fund was established for Davy and Dora, allowing them to remain permanently at Green Gables. Davy enrolled at Avonlea School, where he formed a friendship with Milty Boulter and gradually reformed his mischievous behavior, growing deeply attached to Anne and Marilla.

label: History
value: Diana Barry grew up at Orchard Slope
unit: Diana Barry grew up at Orchard Slope near Green Gables. Shortly after Anne Shirley arrived in Avonlea, the two girls met in the Barry garden and swore an oath of eternal friendship to be bosom friends. Their early companionship involved playing in Mr. Bell's birch grove, creating playhouses, and reading exciting books together. A temporary rift occurred when Diana unwittingly drank three glasses of currant wine at Green Gables thinking it was raspberry cordial; Mrs. Barry forbade the girls to play together until Diana's little sister Minnie May fell severely ill with croup, and Anne saved the child's life. Following this, Mrs. Barry lifted the ban and the girls reunited. Later, Diana accidentally jumped on her wealthy, strict Great-Aunt Josephine during a sleepover, which temporarily enraged the old lady until Anne intervened. Diana attended Avonlea school with Anne, participated in the A.V.I.S. (Avonlea Village Improvement Society), and enjoyed social gatherings together, though she did not pursue higher education at Queen's or Redmond College. Instead, she became engaged to Fred Wright, a young Avonlea farmer, and married him in her eighteenth year in the orchard at Orchard Slope.

Their early companionship involved playing in Mr. Bell's birch grove, creating playhouses, and reading exciting books together. A temporary rift occurred when Diana unwittingly drank three glasses of currant wine at Green Gables thinking it was raspberry cordial; Mrs. Barry forbade the girls to play together until Diana's little sister Minnie May fell severely ill with croup, and Anne saved the child's life. Following this, Mrs. Barry lifted the ban and the girls reunited. Later, Diana accidentally jumped on her wealthy, strict Great-Aunt Josephine during a sleepover, which temporarily enraged the old lady until Anne intervened. Diana attended Avonlea school with Anne, participated in the A.V.I.S. (Avonlea Village Improvement Society), and enjoyed social gatherings together, though she did not pursue higher education at Queen's or Redmond College. Instead, she became engaged to Fred Wright, a young Avonlea farmer, and married him in her eighteenth year in the orchard at Orchard Slope.

She holds orthodox, conventional views, reciting her prayers and lessons dutifully without question.

label: History
value: Dora Keith grew up in East Grafton.
unit: Dora Keith grew up in East Grafton with her sick, widowed mother, Mary Keith, and her twin brother, Davy. Following her mother's death in late autumn, Marilla Cuthbert and Anne Shirley adopted Dora and Davy and brought them to Green Gables. Unlike her troublesome brother, Dora settled quickly into farm life, becoming a favorite helper around the house due to her neatness and reliability. She began attending Avonlea school the following autumn alongside Davy. Although she is occasionally coerced into Davy's misadventures—such as being tricked into walking a pigpen fence or skipping Sunday School—she remains a steadfast, well-behaved child.

label: History
value: Gilbert returned to Avonlea from Alberta.
unit: After returning to Avonlea from Alberta, Gilbert entered Avonlea school and immediately sparked a fierce academic rivalry with Anne Shirley after playfully calling her 'Carrots,' causing her to smash her slate over his head and refuse his apology. Despite his repeated attempts to make peace and his scholastic success at Queen's Academy, Anne maintained her grudge for years. Upon graduating from Queen's, Gilbert selflessly gave up his appointment as teacher at the Avonlea school so that Anne could remain at Green Gables with Marilla Cuthbert. After teaching at White Sands, Gilbert attended Redmond College alongside Anne, where he distinguished himself academically and athletically. He eventually proposed to Anne at Patty's Place, but she rejected him, leaving him heartbroken. Following his graduation with High Honors, Gilbert suffered a life-threatening bout of typhoid fever at his home in Avonlea. Upon his recovery, he learned that Anne had realized her true feelings during his illness, leading to their reconciliation and engagement in Hester Gray's garden.

label: History
value: Mr. Harrison bought the Robert Bell farm next to Green Gables.
unit: Mr. Harrison bought the Robert Bell farm next to Green Gables and moved to Avonlea, quickly gaining a reputation as an eccentric bachelor who kept house for himself and owned a swearing parrot named Ginger. He initially clashed with Anne Shirley after her Jersey cow broke into his oatfield, but the two soon became good friends after Anne mistakenly sold his cow and personally came to apologize and make amends. Unknown to his neighbors, Mr. Harrison was actually married to Emily Scott, from whom he had separated due to domestic disagreements over his habits and his parrot. Following an erroneous note in a local newspaper hinting at his impending marriage, his wife arrived in Avonlea to investigate, leading to their reconciliation and her taking charge of his household.

value: Jane grew up in Avonlea.
unit: Jane grew up in Avonlea and attended the local school with Anne Shirley and Diana Barry, forming a close friendship with them. She later studied at Queen's Academy to become a teacher, subsequently taking the Second Class teacher's course at Redmond College. After graduating, Jane accepted a teaching position in Newbridge. She joined the Avonlea Village Improvement Society and participated in various community events and the girl's Story Club, though her own stories were strictly sensible and free from romance. She was later offered a teaching position out West, where she went to teach. While there, she became engaged to Edward Inglis, a wealthy Winnipeg millionaire, and married him at her family home in Avonlea before leaving for a wedding tour in Europe and settling in a Winnipeg mansion.

value: Josie decided not to seek a teaching position after graduating.
unit: Josie attended the Avonlea school, where she competed with Anne Shirley and other pupils. During a spelling lesson, she was caught peeping in her book by Anne, which led her to spell a word wrong out of embarrassment. At a party hosted by Diana Barry, Josie boasted about her ability to walk a board fence and subsequently dared Anne to walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry's kitchen roof, leading to Anne's fall and a broken ankle. Josie later joined Miss Stacy's class preparing for the entrance examination to Queen's Academy, though she was disgruntled at being cast as a maid of honor rather than the Fairy Queen in a school concert. She passed her entrance examinations, was promoted into the fifth class at school, and went on to attend Queen's Academy, eventually graduating with a Second Class teacher's license alongside her classmates. After graduating, she decided to return to Queen's for further education rather than seek a teaching position.

label: History
value: Lavendar Lewis lived a quiet existence.
unit: Lavendar Lewis lived a quiet, secluded existence in the secluded stone house known as Echo Lodge in Grafton. In her youth, she was engaged to Stephen Irving, but a silly quarrel, compounded by her own sulkiness and their mutual pride, led to a broken engagement, after which Stephen left for the United States. Following her mother's death, Lavendar remained at Echo Lodge, employing a series of young girls whom she sequentially designated 'Charlotta' for convenience. To stave off loneliness, she frequently engaged in imaginative play, setting tea for imaginary guests and inventing a little 'dream-boy' companion. Anne Shirley and Diana Barry accidentally stumbled upon Echo Lodge and became fast friends with Lavendar. Later, Anne introduced Stephen Irving's son, Paul, to Lavendar, which eventually led to Stephen Irving returning to Four Winds to seek her out. Stephen and Lavendar reconciled, overcoming their quarter-century separation, and were married in the garden of Echo Lodge under the honeysuckle arbor. After their wedding, they departed on a trip to the Pacific coast before moving to Boston, keeping Echo Lodge as a summer residence.

unit: Marilla Cuthbert lived a quiet, secluded life at Green Gables with her shy brother Matthew. When Matthew grew older, they decided to adopt an orphan boy from Nova Scotia to help on the farm. Through a miscommunicated message, an eleven-year-old orphan girl named Anne Shirley was sent instead. Although Marilla initially intended to send Anne back, she relented out of pity and a sense of duty, agreeing to raise her. Over the next several years, Marilla navigated the challenges of raising an imaginative, talkative, and impulse-driven child, continually trying to curb Anne's romantic excesses while secretly developing a deep, maternal affection for her. She suffered severe headaches and eventually faced failing eyesight, being warned by an oculist to give up reading and fine sewing to avoid total blindness. Following Matthew's sudden death from a heart attack, Marilla considered selling Green Gables because she could no longer manage the property alone. However, Anne decided to forego her college scholarship to stay in Avonlea and teach locally to support her. Marilla subsequently invited her widowed friend, Rachel Lynde, to move into Green Gables, allowing Anne to attend Redmond College after all.

value: Rachel Lynde is widowed.
unit: Marilla Cuthbert lived a quiet, secluded life at Green Gables with her shy brother Matthew. When Matthew grew older, they decided to adopt an orphan boy from Nova Scotia to help on the farm. Through a miscommunicated message, an eleven-year-old orphan girl named Anne Shirley was sent instead. Although Marilla initially intended to send Anne back, she relented out of pity and a sense of duty, agreeing to raise her. Over the next several years, Marilla navigated the challenges of raising an imaginative, talkative, and impulse-driven child, continually trying to curb Anne's romantic excesses while secretly developing a deep, maternal affection for her. She suffered severe headaches and eventually faced failing eyesight, being warned by an oculist to give up reading and fine sewing to avoid total blindness. Following Matthew's sudden death from a heart attack, Marilla considered selling Green Gables because she could no longer manage the property alone. However, Anne decided to forego her college scholarship to stay in Avonlea and teach locally to support her. Marilla subsequently invited her widowed friend, Rachel Lynde, to move into Green Gables, allowing Anne to attend Redmond College after all.

label: History
value: Matthew Cuthbert lives at Green Gables
unit: Matthew Cuthbert lives at Green Gables in Avonlea with his sister Marilla. Intending to adopt an orphan boy to assist with farm work, Matthew goes to the station only to find a young girl, Anne Shirley, whom he brings home out of compassion. Captivated by her spirit, he persuades Marilla to let her stay. Throughout her upbringing, Matthew remains Anne's gentlest champion, secretly buying her a fashionable dress with puffed sleeves for a school concert and encouraging her romantic nature. As Anne grows older, Matthew's heart condition worsens, preventing him from doing heavy labor. After learning that the Abbey Bank holding his life savings has failed, Matthew suffers a sudden, fatal heart attack and passes away at Green Gables, mourned deeply by his family and neighbors.

label: History
value: Paul Irving arrives in Avonlea
unit: Paul Irving arrives in Avonlea from the United States to live with his grandmother on the shore road. At school, he rapidly becomes a favorite pupil of Anne Shirley, who recognizes him as a kindred spirit and a genius at creative thinking. Paul creates a world of imaginary 'rock people' on the beach, including Nora, the Golden Lady, and the Twin Sailors. He excels in his studies under Anne and Miss Stacy, competing admirably with older students. When his father, Stephen Irving, unexpectedly visits Avonlea, Paul introduces him to Anne, leading eventually to Stephen reuniting with his former love, Miss Lavendar Lewis. Paul warmly accepts Miss Lavendar as his 'Mother Lavendar.' After their wedding, Paul moves to Boston to live with his father and new mother, later travelling abroad for two years of study while publishing his own poetry.

label: History
value: Philippa Gordon first met Anne Shirley
unit: Philippa Gordon first met Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant in Old St. John's Cemetery during their first week as Freshmen at Redmond College. Suffering from acute homesickness, she quickly struck up a close friendship with the two girls. Through her high social standing and radiant charm, she introduced them into Redmond's active social life. Initially, Philippa was torn between two home suitors, Alec and Alonzo, unable to decide between them. During her second year at college, she joined Anne, Priscilla, and Stella Maynard in renting Patty's Place to keep house together under the care of Aunt Jamesina. While vacationing at Prospect Point, she met Jonas Blake, a poor theological student. She fell deeply in love with him, discarded her former wealth-oriented ambitions, and eventually became engaged to him in her Junior year, resolving to support his work as a minister.

label: History
value: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster at Avonlea school.
unit: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster at Avonlea school. During his tenure, he focused much of his time and attention on his older students preparing for Queen's Academy, particularly Prissy Andrews, whom he courted. He maintained poor order in his classroom, periodically attempting strict enforcement through sarcastic punishments and scapegoating. After Anne Shirley arrived at the school, he humiliated her by misspelling her name, forcing her to stand before the blackboard for losing her temper, and later forcing her to sit with Gilbert Blythe for being late. He also took part in the Avonlea Debating Club's winter concert by reciting Mark Antony's oration. At the end of the school year in June, he delivered a farewell speech to the students before leaving his post at Avonlea.

label: History
value: Priscilla Grant met Anne Shirley
unit: Priscilla Grant originally met Anne Shirley while attending Queen's Academy, where she joined Anne's story club. After graduating, she taught school at Carmody for two years before entering Redmond College in Kingsport alongside Anne. The two boarded together at Thirty-Eight St. John's Street and later moved into Patty's Place on Spofford Avenue along with Philippa Gordon, Stella Maynard, and Aunt Jamesina. At Redmond, Priscilla pursued a course in Classics and graduated with Honors. After graduation, she planned to spend time teaching, but retained a lifelong friendship with her college companions.

label: History
value: Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived in Lynde's Hollow near Green Gables.
unit: Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived in Lynde's Hollow near Green Gables, where she kept a watchful eye on all Avonlea happenings. Upon discovering that Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert planned to adopt an orphan boy, she voiced her strong disapproval, and was further astonished when Matthew brought home a girl, Anne Shirley, instead. During her first visit to inspect the child, Mrs. Rachel insulted Anne's appearance, provoking an explosive outburst from the girl. After Anne delivered a humble apology, Mrs. Rachel forgave her and grew quite fond of her over time. Throughout Anne's upbringing, Mrs. Rachel frequently offered unsolicited advice on her discipline and education, recommending that Marilla humor Anne's reluctance to attend school after an incident with Mr. Phillips. She attended a political rally in Charlottetown as a staunch Liberal, accompanied by her husband and Marilla. Later, she helped organize local events such as the Avonlea Debating Club library concert and the Church Aid bazaars.

label: History
value: Roy Gardner attended Redmond College for his Freshman year.
unit: Roy Gardner originally attended Redmond College for his Freshman and Sophomore years before taking two years off to travel in Europe with his mother. Upon his return to complete his Arts degree, he met Anne Shirley in the park on a rainy afternoon when her umbrella turned inside out and he offered his shelter. Deeply taken with her, he began courting her attentively, sending her elegant bouquets of flowers and writing sonnets in her honor. Throughout their Junior and Senior years at Redmond, he remained her devoted escort at college functions, leading many to assume an engagement was inevitable. However, after his proposal to Anne in the park pavilion following their graduation, she realized she did not truly love him in return and rejected his offer. Devastated, Roy bade her farewell and parted from her life.

Upon his return to complete his Arts degree, he met Anne Shirley in the park on a rainy afternoon when her umbrella turned inside out and he offered his shelter. Deeply taken with her, he began courting her attentively, sending her elegant bouquets of flowers and writing sonnets in her honor. Throughout their Junior and Senior years at Redmond, he remained her devoted escort at college functions, leading many to assume an engagement was inevitable. However, after his proposal to Anne in the park pavilion following their graduation, she realized she did not truly love him in return and rejected his offer. Devastated, Roy bade her farewell and parted from her life.

label: History
value: Ruby Gillis grew up in Avonlea.
unit: Ruby Gillis grew up in Avonlea as one of Anne Shirley's classmates and friends. She attended Queen's Academy to study for a teaching license and joined the Story Club and the Village Improvement Society. After graduating from Queen's, she taught at the Carmody school for a time and later obtained the White Sands school. During a winter teaching term, she suffered an attack of congestion that developed into galloping consumption. Despite her failing health, Ruby maintained a bright, hopeful facade throughout the summer, denying the severity of her illness. Eventually, she admitted her fear of death to Anne during a quiet evening at her home. Shortly afterward, Ruby passed away peacefully in her sleep and was buried in the Avonlea graveyard.

label: History
value: Miss Muriel Stacy is engaged as the new teacher for Avonlea school.
unit: Miss Muriel Stacy is engaged as the new teacher for Avonlea school, becoming the first female teacher the community has ever had. She introduces various new educational methods, such as physical culture exercises, bi-weekly recitation and dialogue afternoons, and 'field' afternoons in the woods to study nature and write compositions. In the fall, she organizes a successful student concert to raise money for a schoolhouse flag. She encourages Anne Shirley in her studies and compositions, and later forms an advanced class after school to prepare interested students for the entrance examination into Queen's Academy. Though offered a position in her home district's grade school, she decides to remain in Avonlea to see her students through their preparation. She drills her entrance class thoroughly through the following school year, after which she leaves her rule at Avonlea school at the end of June when her pupils take their examinations.
